title: Colloquial Contractions
summary: Understand common Brazilian spoken forms like pra, tá, tô, cadê, né, and cê while controlling register.

sections.heading: Everyday spoken reductions
sections.body: Brazilian speech frequently reduces common words. These forms are natural in conversation, messages, songs, and dialogue, but not always appropriate in formal writing.

examples.en: I'm going to the beach tomorrow.

sections.heading: Interaction markers
sections.body: Words like **né**, **tá**, **viu**, and **então** manage conversation: checking agreement, softening commands, or marking transitions.

examples.en: Call me when you arrive, okay?

examples.pt: Então, a gente precisa decidir hoje.
examples.en: So, we need to decide today.

sections.heading: Cadê and cê
sections.body: **Cadê** means 'where is/are?' and is extremely common. **Cê** is a reduced form of você in many regions, but it is informal and should be avoided in careful writing.

keyPoints: Tô, tá, pra, cadê, né, and cê are normal in informal Brazilian speech.
Use full forms in academic, professional, or formal writing.
Interaction markers like né and tá help manage tone.

commonMistakes.wrong: Eu tô disponível para a reunião formal.
commonMistakes.right: Estou disponível para a reunião formal.
commonMistakes.note: Use full forms in formal contexts.
As subject of an infinitive, use eu in standard Portuguese.
